title: Tensor product of a geometrically normal algebra and a normal algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $A$ and $B$ be commutative $k$-algebras. Assume $A$ is geometrically normal over $k$, meaning that for every field extension $E/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] the commutative tensor-product algebra $A\otimes_k E$ is a normal ring. Assume $B$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then $A\otimes_k B$ is a normal ring: each of its prime localizations is an integrally closed domain. Tensor products are commutative tensor-product algebras [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with $(a\otimes b)(a^{\prime}\otimes b^{\prime})=aa^{\prime}\otimes bb^{\prime}$ and unit $1\otimes1$. No Noetherian, finite-type, domain or nonzero hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or $B$.

proof.text: We first record two elementary consequences of the normal-ring definition, to be used below. If R is normal and T is multiplicative, a prime Q of T^{-1}R contracts to a prime p of R disjoint from T, and (T^{-1}R)_Q = R_p: the mutually inverse fraction maps send (r/t)/(u/v) to rv/(tu), and r/s to (r/1)/(s/1). Thus T^{-1}R is normal. Also R is reduced: for a nonzero nilpotent x choose a maximal ideal p containing its proper annihilator. Then x/1 is nonzero in R_p (otherwise some s outside p annihilates x) and nilpotent, contradicting that R_p is a domain. These arguments include the zero ring, which has no primes.

Geometric normality is preserved by localization: for each extension E/k, the tensor product of a localization of A with E is the localization of A tensor E at the images of the same denominators, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], applied with R=A, R'=T^{-1}A and D=A tensor_k E. The identification (A tensor_k E) tensor_A T^{-1}A = T^{-1}A tensor_k E sends (a tensor e) tensor(a'/t) to (aa'/t) tensor e; its inverse sends (a/t) tensor e to (1 tensor e) tensor(a/t). Bilinearity and the A-balancing relation verify that these maps are well-defined inverse ring maps. The swap sends a tensor e to e tensor a and is inverse to itself, by the tensor universal property. Step 1 gives normality of this localization. In particular A is normal by E=k, and every A_p is geometrically normal.

Fix a prime r of A tensor_k B, and let p and q be its contractions to A and B. The images of A minus p and B minus q avoid r. Apply the maps of Step 2 with E replaced by B, then interchange the factors and apply them with A replaced by B and E replaced by A_p. Twice applying [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] therefore identifies A_p tensor_k B_q with the localization of A tensor_k B obtained by inverting these images. Localizing once more at the prime induced by r gives exactly (A tensor_k B)_r, by the fraction formulas in Step 1. A_p and B_q are normal domains by the hypotheses and Step 2, and A_p is geometrically normal. It therefore suffices to prove normality of A tensor_k B when A and B are normal domains and A is geometrically normal. If either original algebra is zero there is no r and the conclusion is vacuous. For the remainder of the proof A and B denote these domains; write K=Frac(A) and L=Frac(B).

source.place: Tag 06DF first paragraph: reduction to domains

proof.text: For any finitely generated k-subalgebra D of B, apply [lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite] to X=Spec D and the degree-one extension Frac(D)/Frac(D). By [def-fin-normalization-extension] its source is Spec N, where N is the integral closure of D in Frac(D). The finite-morphism definition makes N finite as a D-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal], N is an integrally closed domain with fraction field Frac(D). Embed Frac(D) into L using D subset B. Every element of N is integral over D, hence over B by the same monic equation, and belongs to B by [lem-weil-pbc-normal-ring-integrally-closed-total] applied to the domain B. Thus N is a normal k-subalgebra of B containing D; normality of all its prime localizations follows from [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. It is finite type over k: if d_1,...,d_h generate D as a k-algebra and n_1,...,n_m generate N as a D-module, these elements together generate N as a k-algebra. Consequently the collection I of all normal finite-type k-subalgebras of B is nonempty, covers B, and is directed: for two members take D generated by the union of their finite generating sets and perform this construction. I is a set of subalgebras, hence a small directed poset after choosing the universe of k,A,B.

source.place: Tag 06DF second paragraph; Tags 0335 (proposition-ubiquity-nagata), 0334 (proposition-nagata-universally-japanese), expanded using the existing finite-normalization theorem

proof.text: The inclusions A tensor_k B_i into A tensor_k B, for B_i in I, exhibit the latter as their filtered colimit of rings. Indeed tensoring an inclusion over k is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat] and the injectivity definition of flatness. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors and all its B-coordinates lie in one B_i. For a compatible family of ring maps out of A tensor_k B_i, define its value on an element using any stage containing that element; a common upper stage proves independence, addition and multiplication, and uniqueness follows from the union. This proves the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-normal-ring], it suffices to prove the domain case with B finite type over k. The rest of the proof establishes precisely that case; Step 11 then returns to the original algebras.

source.place: Tag 06DF second paragraph: filtered-colimit reduction to finite-type B

proof.text: Assume henceforth that B is finite type. By Step 2, K is geometrically normal, so K tensor_k E is reduced for every field extension E/k by Step 1. If k has positive characteristic, apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-reduced-extension-separable]; if k has characteristic zero, apply [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable]. In either case K/k is separable in the sense that every finitely generated intermediate field K_i/k is separably generated. These K_i form a small nonempty directed poset and their union is K: the subfield generated by the union of two finite sets contains the corresponding two intermediate fields.

source.place: Tag 06DF final paragraph; Tag 030T (lemma-subalgebra-separable); separability criterion and characteristic-zero case

proof.text: For each K_i, [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-fraction-field-of-smooth-algebra] supplies a smooth k-subalgebra D_i of K_i with fraction field K_i. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], B tensor_k D_i is smooth over B. It is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-normal-ring-normal], since B is normal. The explicit maps of Step 2, with A=D_i and E=B, and the factor swap identify B tensor_k K_i with its localization at the nonzero elements of D_i, so Step 1 makes B tensor_k K_i normal. Swap factors to obtain normality of K_i tensor_k B. Field-flatness makes each K_i tensor_k B inject into K tensor_k B. Every element is a finite sum of pure tensors, whose finitely many K-coordinates lie in one K_i. Given compatible ring maps from these stages, evaluate an element at any stage containing it. A common larger intermediate field proves independence of the chosen stage and preservation of addition and multiplication; coverage proves uniqueness. This verifies that K tensor_k B is their filtered colimit. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-normal-ring] proves that K tensor_k B is normal. Independently, A tensor_k L is normal by the original geometric-normality hypothesis, since L/k is a field extension.

Put C=A tensor_k B, C_A=K tensor_k B and C_B=A tensor_k L. The maps C to C_A and C to C_B are injective: tensor the inclusions A subset K and B subset L over the field k, using the flatness statement and definition. They are localizations by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change]. Their inverted elements are nonzerodivisors of C: multiplication by any nonzero a in A, or b in B, is injective before tensoring and remains injective afterward. By Step 7, C_A and C_B are normal, hence reduced by Step 1; therefore their subring C is reduced. C_A is finite type over K, generated by the same finitely many B-generators, so it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (a field has only two ideals). It has finitely many minimal primes by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes].

source.place: Tag 06DF third paragraph, and fourth paragraph localization setup

proof.text: The map A to C is flat. For an injection of A-modules M to N, the identification M tensor_A C = M tensor_k B (m tensor(a tensor b) maps to am tensor b, with inverse m tensor b maps to m tensor(1 tensor b)) identifies the induced map with tensoring the underlying injection of k-vector spaces by B. This is injective by field-flatness. For a minimal prime r of C, going down [lem-sc-flat-going-down] applied to (0) subset r intersect A yields a prime r' subset r contracting to (0). Minimality forces r'=r. Hence every minimal prime of C avoids A minus zero. Such primes extend injectively to minimal primes of C_A: extension and contraction are inverse, since a fraction c/s belongs to the extended prime exactly when c belongs to the original prime; any prime strictly below the extended prime would contract to a strictly smaller prime of C. Thus C has finitely many minimal primes by Step 8.

Both C_A and C_B embed in Q(C), since their denominators are nonzerodivisors of C. Moreover Q(C_A)=Q(C)=Q(C_B): localizing at a subset of the nonzerodivisors preserves nonzerodivisors, and if c/s is a nonzerodivisor in this localization, c is already a nonzerodivisor in C, since localization at nonzerodivisors is injective. Also K tensor_k L embeds in Q(C), by inverting both sets of denominators. Inside this ring C_A intersect C_B=C. To check the equality, split K=A direct-sum U and L=B direct-sum V as k-vector spaces: choose a basis of K/A and lift it to K to obtain U, and do the same for L/B; vector-space bases exist by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. Bilinearity gives K tensor L=(A tensor B) direct-sum (U tensor B) direct-sum (A tensor V) direct-sum (U tensor V); the projections to these four summands are induced by the projections of the split vector spaces. C_A comprises the first two summands and C_B the first and third, so their intersection is the first summand. Now let x in Q(C) be integral over C. Its monic equation is also a monic equation over C_A and C_B. By [lem-weil-pbc-normal-ring-integrally-closed-total] and Step 7, x belongs to both rings, hence to C. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-normal-iff-integrally-closed-total-fractions], reducedness and finiteness of the minimal primes from Steps 8 and 9 imply that C is normal.

source.place: Tag 06DF fourth paragraph, intersection argument expanded; Tag 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal)

proof.text: Step 10 proves the normal-domain case for each finite-type normal B_i of Step 4, with the same geometrically normal A. Step 5 and the filtered-colimit normality theorem therefore prove the domain case for arbitrary B. Apply this domain case to A_p and B_q in Step 3 and then use the prime-localization calculation there: every (A tensor_k B)_r is an integrally closed domain. This is exactly normality of the original tensor product. No finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis survives the reductions, and no domain or nonzero hypothesis is imposed on the original A or B.
